summary: LUNAR COMMAND is an interactive 3D game simulating space exploration, survival, and engineering activities intended for kids. Players create their own rockets, explore Earth, the Moon, and Mars, design space stations, and control vital elements such as oxygen, water, food, and energy. Integrating realistic physics, missions, and DONKI space weather provided by NASA, the game incorporates real-life situations related to radiation, gravity, and astronaut survival. LUNAR COMMAND inspires players to think creatively and critically, work in a team, and solve problems while encouraging kids to become astronauts, scientists, and engineers.
details:
Project Details — LUNAR COMMAND

LUNAR COMMAND is an interactive 3D space exploration and engineering simulator for children aged 7-12 to learn about space exploration in a fun and engaging way.

In LUNAR COMMAND, players can build and launch rockets, explore Earth, Moon and Mars, build space stations and planetary settlements, and manage vital resources such as oxygen, water, food, power and radiation protection. Using realistic planetary gravity, rocketry physics and mission-related tasks, the simulator allows players to learn about the underlying principles of space missions.

One of the unique features is the use of NASA DONKI data about space weather and its influence on astronauts' safety.

The project is being built with Google AI Studio, JavaScript/TypeScript, browser 3D technologies, physics simulation and NASA APIs. Our main focus in the development of the game is scientific accuracy, accessibility, intuitive interface and educational value.

The uniqueness of our project lies in space engineering, planetary exploration, survival and scientific data used in one place.

Our goal is to create a connection between theoretical knowledge and practice allowing kids to experiment, analyze, solve problems and be creative.
